clinical_notes: a middle-aged, 45-year-old male patient with longstanding history of human immunodeficiency virus (hiv) infection and severe immunosuppression (4 cd+ cells/mmc) unresponsive to antiretroviral therapy, was hospitalised because of malaise, diarrhoea, weight loss and metabolic acidosis, without specific respiratory symptoms. normally aerated lungs with a 3-cm subpleural consolidation in the right infraclavicular region, showing central cavitation (detailed view in c), suggesting a possible diagnosis of tuberculosis.
